title: Library management
scopeHtml: Scope: Books vs copies, loans, fines, reservations, concurrent checkout. Questions are still to be written.

notes.title: Requirements
notes.html:
Design a library management system: members search books, borrow copies, return them (with a fine if late), and reserve a title when all copies are out.

Clarify: one library or a branch network? Are there multiple copies of one title (yes)? Loan period (14 days), per-member limit (3), fine rate (2 per day)? Reservation queue (first come first served)? Who uses it: members only, or librarians too? (Here: one library, books vs copies, limit 3, 14 days, fine per day, FIFO waitlist with notification.)

Worked example. "Clean Code" has 1 copy. Asha borrows it on 1 Jan, due 15 Jan. Ravi reserves it. Asha returns it on 21 Jan: 6 days late x 2 = 12 fine. Ravi is notified; nobody else can borrow it until Ravi does (or the hold lapses). A library with 50,000 titles and 120,000 copies is tiny data, so correctness matters far more than performance.

Industry examples. Koha and Evergreen (open-source library systems), OverDrive/Libby (digital lending with holds queues), university library systems, and the same lending model in equipment rental or Blockbuster-style rentals.

Everyday analogy. A school library card: you can take 3 books, each for two weeks, and if a book is out you can join the waiting list.

Common interview traps.

  • Modelling a book and a physical copy as the same thing (cannot have two copies with different states).
  • Skipping the loan limit and reservations because they are "extra"; they are the interesting rules.
  • Using the real clock so the fine cannot be tested.

notes.title: Core entities
notes.html:
• Book (title level): isbn, title, author. Searchable.
  • BookCopy (physical item): copyId, which book, and who has it (null = on shelf).
  • Member: id, name, current loans.
  • Loan: copy, member, due date.
  • FinePolicy (interface): late days to amount.
  • ReservationListener (interface): callback when a reserved title is free.
  • Library: facade holding catalogues, members and waitlists; all rules live here.

The key insight is two-level inventory: a title has many copies; search works on titles, checkout works on copies.

Decision gravity. Splitting Book/BookCopy is a one-way-ish data-model door: merging them later means a schema migration and rewriting every query. Fines and notifications are behind interfaces, which are cheap to change.

Everyday analogy. A bookshop catalogue lists "Harry Potter" once, while the shelf holds five physical copies with different wear.

Common interview traps.

  • Search returning copies instead of titles (duplicate results).
  • Storing the due date on the copy rather than on the loan; history is lost.

notes.title: Class diagram
notes.html:
+----------------------------------------------+
| Library                                      |
| books:     Map<isbn, Book>                   |
| copies:    Map<isbn, List<BookCopy>>         |
| members:   Map<id, Member>                   |
| waitlist:  Map<isbn, Deque<memberId>>        |
| today: Supplier<LocalDate>                   |
| search(q) / checkout(m,isbn) / giveBack(m,c) |
| reserve(m,isbn)                              |
+--+----------+-----------+--------------------+
   |          |           |
   v          v           v
+------+  +----------+  +--------+      <<interface>>
| Book |  | BookCopy |  | Member |      FinePolicy ---- PerDayFine
|isbn  |<-|copyId    |  |loans[] |      fine(daysLate)
|title |  |borrowedBy|  +---+----+
|author|  +----------+      |            <<interface>>
+------+                    v            ReservationListener
                        +------+         onAvailable(member, book)
                        | Loan |
                        |copy, |
                        |member|
                        |due   |
                        +------+

How to read it. Library is a Facade: callers use four methods, and it enforces limit, waitlist order and fines. Money and time policy are injected.

Common interview traps.

  • Splitting rules across Member and Book classes so no single place guarantees "limit 3".
  • Making Library a singleton with static state (untestable). Pass it around.

notes.title: Key patterns
notes.html:
• Facade (Library): one entry point hides catalogue, loans and queue coordination. Why: a small API with all rules in one place. Alternative: separate LoanService, CatalogService, ReservationService (better at larger scale; each can be owned by a team). Reversible.
  • Strategy (FinePolicy): fine formula (flat per day, capped at book price, free for staff) swappable. Why: policy changes often; code should not.
  • Observer (ReservationListener): the library announces "a reserved title is back" without knowing how (email, SMS, push). Reuse the Notification system (P8) behind it.
  • Dependency injection of time (Supplier<LocalDate>): tests can move 20 days forward instantly.
  • FIFO queue (ArrayDeque) per title: fair reservations.

Industry examples. OverDrive "holds" use the same FIFO queue with a "you have 72 hours to borrow" window; hotel and car rental systems use identical title/unit separation (room type vs room).

Everyday analogy. The "Next customer" ticket machine at a bank: first number called, first served.

Common interview traps.

  • Letting anyone borrow a reserved copy because the check only looks at "available".
  • Hardcoding 14, 3 and the fine into methods; at least use named constants.

notes.title: Code
notes.html:
Full runnable file Main.java (catalogue, limit, fines, waitlist and a concurrent checkout test):

import java.time.LocalDate;
import java.time.temporal.ChronoUnit;
import java.util.*;
import java.util.function.Supplier;
import java.util.stream.Collectors;

/** A title (what you search for) vs a copy (what you physically borrow). Two classes, not one. */
class Book {
    final String isbn, title, author;
    Book(String isbn, String title, String author) { this.isbn = isbn; this.title = title; this.author = author; }
}

class BookCopy {
    final String copyId; final Book book;
    private String borrowedBy;                 // null = on the shelf
    BookCopy(String copyId, Book book) { this.copyId = copyId; this.book = book; }
    boolean isAvailable() { return borrowedBy == null; }
    void borrow(String memberId) { borrowedBy = memberId; }
    void giveBack() { borrowedBy = null; }
}

class Member {
    final String id, name; final List<Loan> loans = new ArrayList<>();
    Member(String id, String name) { this.id = id; this.name = name; }
}

class Loan {
    final BookCopy copy; final Member member; final LocalDate dueDate;
    Loan(BookCopy copy, Member member, LocalDate dueDate) { this.copy = copy; this.member = member; this.dueDate = dueDate; }
}

/** Strategy for fines so policy changes do not touch Library. */
interface FinePolicy { long fine(long daysLate); }
class PerDayFine implements FinePolicy {
    private final long perDay; PerDayFine(long perDay) { this.perDay = perDay; }
    public long fine(long daysLate) { return daysLate <= 0 ? 0 : daysLate * perDay; }
}

/** Observer: told when a reserved title becomes free. */
interface ReservationListener { void onAvailable(String memberId, Book book); }

class Library {
    static final int MAX_LOANS = 3, LOAN_DAYS = 14;
    private final Map<String, Book> books = new HashMap<>();
    private final Map<String, List<BookCopy>> copies = new HashMap<>();       // isbn -> copies
    private final Map<String, Member> members = new HashMap<>();
    private final Map<String, Deque<String>> waitlist = new HashMap<>();      // isbn -> queued member ids
    private final Supplier<LocalDate> today; private final FinePolicy fines; private final ReservationListener listener;

    Library(Supplier<LocalDate> today, FinePolicy fines, ReservationListener listener) {
        this.today = today; this.fines = fines; this.listener = listener;
    }
    synchronized void addBook(Book b, int nCopies) {
        books.put(b.isbn, b);
        List<BookCopy> l = copies.computeIfAbsent(b.isbn, k -> new ArrayList<>());
        for (int i = 0; i < nCopies; i++) l.add(new BookCopy(b.isbn + "-" + (l.size() + 1), b));
    }
    synchronized void addMember(Member m) { members.put(m.id, m); }

    synchronized List<Book> search(String q) {
        String s = q.toLowerCase();
        return books.values().stream().filter(b -> b.title.toLowerCase().contains(s) || b.author.toLowerCase().contains(s))
                .sorted(Comparator.comparing(b -> b.title)).collect(Collectors.toList());
    }

    /** Whole check-out is one critical section so two members cannot take the last copy. */
    synchronized Loan checkout(String memberId, String isbn) {
        Member m = members.get(memberId);
        if (m == null) throw new IllegalArgumentException("unknown member");
        if (m.loans.size() >= MAX_LOANS) throw new IllegalStateException("loan limit reached");
        Deque<String> q = waitlist.getOrDefault(isbn, new ArrayDeque<>());
        if (!q.isEmpty() && !q.peekFirst().equals(memberId)) throw new IllegalStateException("reserved for someone else");
        BookCopy copy = copies.getOrDefault(isbn, List.of()).stream().filter(BookCopy::isAvailable).findFirst()
                .orElseThrow(() -> new IllegalStateException("no copy available"));
        if (!q.isEmpty()) q.pollFirst();
        copy.borrow(memberId);
        Loan loan = new Loan(copy, m, today.get().plusDays(LOAN_DAYS));
        m.loans.add(loan);
        return loan;
    }

    /** Returns the fine owed (0 if on time). */
    synchronized long giveBack(String memberId, String copyId) {
        Member m = members.get(memberId);
        Loan loan = m.loans.stream().filter(l -> l.copy.copyId.equals(copyId)).findFirst()
                .orElseThrow(() -> new IllegalStateException("not borrowed by this member"));
        m.loans.remove(loan);
        loan.copy.giveBack();
        long late = ChronoUnit.DAYS.between(loan.dueDate, today.get());
        Deque<String> q = waitlist.get(loan.copy.book.isbn);
        if (q != null && !q.isEmpty()) listener.onAvailable(q.peekFirst(), loan.copy.book);
        return fines.fine(late);
    }

    synchronized void reserve(String memberId, String isbn) {
        boolean anyFree = copies.getOrDefault(isbn, List.of()).stream().anyMatch(BookCopy::isAvailable);
        if (anyFree) throw new IllegalStateException("copy is available, just check it out");
        waitlist.computeIfAbsent(isbn, k -> new ArrayDeque<>()).addLast(memberId);
    }
}

public class Main {
    static void check(boolean c, String msg) { if (!c) throw new AssertionError(msg); }

    public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception {
        LocalDate[] day = {LocalDate.of(2026, 1, 1)};
        List<String> notices = new ArrayList<>();
        Library lib = new Library(() -> day[0], new PerDayFine(2), (mid, b) -> notices.add(mid + ":" + b.title));
        lib.addBook(new Book("111", "Clean Code", "Martin"), 1);
        lib.addBook(new Book("222", "Effective Java", "Bloch"), 2);
        lib.addBook(new Book("333", "Refactoring", "Fowler"), 1);
        lib.addBook(new Book("444", "DDIA", "Kleppmann"), 1);
        lib.addMember(new Member("m1", "Asha")); lib.addMember(new Member("m2", "Ravi"));

        check(lib.search("java").size() == 1 && lib.search("MARTIN").size() == 1, "search title/author");
        Loan l = lib.checkout("m1", "111");
        lib.reserve("m2", "111");
        lib.checkout("m1", "222"); lib.checkout("m1", "333");
        boolean limited = false;
        try { lib.checkout("m1", "444"); } catch (IllegalStateException e) { limited = true; }
        check(limited, "max 3 loans");

        day[0] = day[0].plusDays(20);                         // 6 days late
        check(lib.giveBack("m1", l.copy.copyId) == 12, "6 days * 2");
        check(notices.equals(List.of("m2:Clean Code")), "waitlist notified");
        boolean blocked = false;
        try { lib.checkout("m1", "111"); } catch (IllegalStateException e) { blocked = true; }
        check(blocked, "copy held for m2");
        lib.checkout("m2", "111");

        // concurrency: 2 copies of "222" minus 1 taken = 1 left; 20 members race, exactly one wins
        for (int i = 0; i < 20; i++) lib.addMember(new Member("x" + i, "x"));
        java.util.concurrent.atomic.AtomicInteger won = new java.util.concurrent.atomic.AtomicInteger();
        Thread[] ts = new Thread[20];
        for (int i = 0; i < 20; i++) {
            final String id = "x" + i;
            ts[i] = new Thread(() -> { try { lib.checkout(id, "222"); won.incrementAndGet(); } catch (IllegalStateException ignored) {} });
            ts[i].start();
        }
        for (Thread t : ts) t.join();
        check(won.get() == 1, "one copy left, winners=" + won.get());
        System.out.println("P12 OK");
    }
}

The core in Kotlin:

import java.time.LocalDate
import java.time.temporal.ChronoUnit

class Book(val isbn: String, val title: String, val author: String)
class BookCopy(val copyId: String, val book: Book) { var borrowedBy: String? = null }
class Loan(val copy: BookCopy, val memberId: String, val due: LocalDate)

class Library(private val today: () -> LocalDate,
              private val finePerDay: Long = 2,
              private val onAvailable: (String, Book) -> Unit = { _, _ -> }) {
    private val copies = HashMap<String, MutableList<BookCopy>>()
    private val loans = HashMap<String, MutableList<Loan>>()       // memberId -> loans
    private val waitlist = HashMap<String, ArrayDeque<String>>()   // isbn -> member ids

    @Synchronized fun checkout(memberId: String, isbn: String): Loan {
        val mine = loans.getOrPut(memberId) { mutableListOf() }
        check(mine.size < 3) { "loan limit reached" }
        val q = waitlist[isbn]
        check(q.isNullOrEmpty() || q.first() == memberId) { "reserved for someone else" }
        val copy = copies[isbn].orEmpty().firstOrNull { it.borrowedBy == null }
            ?: error("no copy available")
        q?.removeFirstOrNull()
        copy.borrowedBy = memberId
        return Loan(copy, memberId, today().plusDays(14)).also { mine += it }
    }

    @Synchronized fun giveBack(memberId: String, copyId: String): Long {
        val mine = loans.getValue(memberId)
        val loan = mine.first { it.copy.copyId == copyId }
        mine.remove(loan); loan.copy.borrowedBy = null
        waitlist[loan.copy.book.isbn]?.firstOrNull()?.let { onAvailable(it, loan.copy.book) }
        val late = ChronoUnit.DAYS.between(loan.due, today())
        return if (late > 0) late * finePerDay else 0
    }
}

Walk-through. Return on day 21 of a loan due on day 14 gives between(due, today) = 6, times 2 = 12. Returning on day 14 or earlier gives 0 or negative, which the policy maps to 0.

Common interview traps.

  • Computing "days late" with Date arithmetic and time zones; use LocalDate.
  • Notifying the listener while holding internal locks in a way that lets it call back into Library and deadlock (here the lock is reentrant, but production listeners should enqueue instead).
  • Removing the member from the waitlist only on checkout but never expiring stale holds.

notes.title: Run and test
notes.html:
javac Main.java && java -ea Main
# prints: P12 OK

The test fixes the date to 1 Jan 2026 and moves it. It asserts: case-insensitive search by title and author; the fourth concurrent loan is refused (limit 3); returning 6 days late costs 12; the waitlisted member is notified and another member's checkout is blocked while the copy is held; and 20 threads racing for the last copy of a title produce exactly one winner.

Common interview traps.

  • No negative test (limit exceeded, copy unavailable). The error paths are the rules.
  • Forgetting to test "return a book you did not borrow".

notes.title: Concurrency
notes.html:
Race to avoid: two members call checkout for the last copy at the same moment. Both see isAvailable() true, both mark it borrowed, and one copy ends up loaned twice. Same for the member limit: two simultaneous checkouts could both pass loans.size() < 3.

  • Shown: every state-changing method on Library is synchronized. The check (limit, waitlist, availability) and the update (mark borrowed, add loan) are one atomic step. The 20-thread test yields exactly one winner. For a library with perhaps 1 to 10 checkouts per second, a single lock is more than enough.
  • Finer-grained: lock per ISBN for copy assignment, plus per-member lock for the limit, always taken in a fixed order (member id then isbn) to avoid deadlock. Needed only at very high contention, which a library will never see.
  • Database version: UPDATE copy SET borrowed_by=? WHERE copy_id=? AND borrowed_by IS NULL and check rows affected; a unique partial index on (copy_id) WHERE returned_at IS NULL on the loans table makes double-loan impossible even with bugs. Member limit: SELECT ... FOR UPDATE on the member row, or a constraint trigger.
  • Reads (search) can use a snapshot or cache without the write lock; the catalogue changes rarely.

Incident pattern. Duplicate loans appear after a retry: the mobile app times out, the user taps again, two loans created. Symptom: member shows 2 loans for the same copy. Fix: idempotency key per checkout request, plus the unique index.

Decision gravity. A coarse lock is the correct first choice: reversible, simple, and impossible to deadlock. Do not optimise concurrency in a system whose peak is a few requests a second.

Everyday analogy. One librarian at the desk handles one person at a time, so the last copy cannot be handed to two people.

Common interview traps.

  • Locking on the Book object rather than on the shared inventory (different Book instances for the same isbn).
  • Checking availability in one synchronized method and loaning in another (check-then-act gap).

notes.title: Follow-ups
notes.html:
• Renewals: extend the due date once, only if no one is waitlisted.
  • Reservation expiry: if the head of the waitlist does not borrow within 3 days, move to the next (scheduled job or lazy check).
  • Lost / damaged copy: copy state LOST with a replacement fee.
  • Roles: librarian adds books, members borrow; permissions.
  • Search at scale: inverted index or Elasticsearch / Postgres full-text instead of scanning (search here is O(n) over titles).
  • Branches: copies have a branchId; inter-branch transfers.
  • Digital lending: copies are licences; same hold queue, different limits.
  • Notifications: due-soon and overdue reminders through the Notification system (P8).

Common interview traps.

  • Linear search presented as production-ready; say what you would index.
  • Letting fines accumulate unbounded; cap at the book price or block borrowing above a threshold.

notes.title: Summary
notes.html:
• Two-level model: Book (title, searchable) and BookCopy (physical, borrowable); loans record due date.
  • Library is a facade enforcing limit, FIFO reservations and fines; fine policy and notifications are injected (Strategy, Observer).
  • Inject the clock so late-fee logic is testable.
  • Make check-and-update atomic (synchronized here, conditional SQL update plus unique index in a database).
  • Extensions: renewals, reservation expiry, branches, search index, reminders.
